 VA pays each month’s disability benefit on the 1st of the following month. When the 1st falls on a weekend or a federal holiday, payment is moved to the last business day before it.¹
 The first payment on the 2027 schedule is Thursday, Dec. 31, 2026 (for December). It comes early because Jan. 1 is New Year’s Day,² and the final payment under the 2027 pay rate structure is due on December 1, 2027.
 Not sure what your payment will be? Try our VA disability calculator or check out our 2027 VA disability rates and pay charts.

 2027 VA Disability Pay Dates 
 VA pays on the 1st of the month after the benefit month, or on the last business day before the 1st when the 1st falls on a weekend or federal holiday.¹ These dates apply that rule to the 2027 calendar. If you’re managing benefits for a veteran or family member, mark these dates below.

 Early deposits create months with no payments and months with two payments. In 2027:
 No deposit: January, May, and August. The previous payment arrived on Dec. 31, Apr. 30, or Jul. 30.
 Two deposits: April (Apr. 1 and Apr. 30), July (Jul. 1 and Jul. 30), and December (Dec. 1 and Dec. 30 for the 2028 payment schedule year ).
 An early deposit isn’t extra money. The next payment arrives sooner, so the following calendar month has none. If rent or a mortgage is due on the 1st, set aside part of an early deposit to cover it.

 VA Early Pay Dates: Your Bank May Show It Early 
 Some banks and credit unions, such as USAA and Navy Federal, may post VA deposits one to two business days before the dates above. That’s the bank’s choice, not VA’s date.
 Here is a list of other early-pay banks and direct deposit calendars .
 VA sets no time of day, so when the deposit posts depends on your bank’s processing. You can also opt in to a text alert each time a recurring VA payment arrives through your VA.gov profile.³

 Why VA Pays a Month Behind 
 Think of it like a paycheck for a month you’ve already worked. VA’s benefit covers the month that just ended and is paid at the start of the next one.⁴ January’s benefit arrives Feb. 1. December’s arrives around Dec. 31.
 New awards follow the same logic: payment can’t begin before the first day of the month following the award’s effective date.¹
 The weekend rule works like a payday that falls on a Saturday: it moves earlier, never later. When the 1st is a Saturday or Sunday, VA aims to pay the Friday before. When it’s a legal holiday, such as Jan. 1, VA aims to pay on the weekday before the holiday.¹

 The 2027 Cost-of-Living Increase 
 VA disability pay is tied to an annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) announced by the Social Security Administration, which helps your payment keep up with rising prices. When a new increase takes effect, it shows up in your monthly payment, usually starting with the December payment.⁴
 VA Disability Pay Date FAQs 
 Below are some of the most common questions about VA disability pay dates.
 What time of day are VA disability checks deposited? 
 VA disability pay typically arrives on the dates above, but there’s no set time of day it will hit your account. When you receive funds typically depends on your bank’s processing times.
 Note: If you receive more than one VA benefit via direct deposit , VA pays them all into one account. VA required anyone with benefits going to separate accounts to consolidate them by April 20, 2024, and combined the accounts of anyone who didn’t.⁵
 What should I do if I don’t receive my VA disability payment? 
 Start by checking your payment history and direct deposit details. Sign in to VA.gov to see your recent payments, and confirm the bank information in your VA.gov profile.³ If your payment still hasn’t arrived, call the Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Help Line at :
 800-827-1000 (TTY: 711)
Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET.³
 If it’s your first payment after a decision showing at least a 10% rating, VA says to call if it hasn’t arrived within 15 days.³
 Does VA still mail paper checks? 
 Mostly no. Executive Order 14247 directed Treasury to stop issuing paper checks for federal benefit payments starting Sept. 30, 2025,⁵ and Treasury said most of those payments must now be electronic.⁵ The order allows exceptions, including for people without access to banking services.⁵ Treasury points anyone still getting a check to MyMoney.gov/FederalPayments.⁵
 What other VA benefits impact my VA disability payment? 
 Monthly VA benefit payments include VA disability compensation, education, pension, and survivors benefits.³
 Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) 
 Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) and Parents’ Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) are tax-free benefits for surviving spouses, children, or parents of service members who died while on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training. Survivors of veterans who died from a service-connected illness or injury may also qualify. Only Parents’ DIC has an income limit.
 Veterans and Survivors Pension Compensation 
 VA offers two pension benefits that provide monthly income to wartime veterans and survivors with limited income.
 Veterans Pension : A tax-free monthly benefit for some wartime veterans with limited or no income who meet age or disability requirements.
 Survivors Pension : A monthly benefit for the unmarried surviving spouse and unmarried children of a Veteran with wartime service, when household income and net worth are within limits.
 Aid and Attendance and Housebound Benefits 
 Aid and Attendance and Housebound benefits are tax-free and are added to your monthly VA pension.
 Aid and Attendance : For people who need another person’s help with daily activities such as bathing, feeding or dressing, stay in bed much of the day due to illness, live in a nursing home due to disability-related loss of abilities, or have severely limited eyesight.
 Housebound Benefits: For people who spend most of their time at home because of a permanent disability. You can’t receive both benefits at the same time.
 Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) 
 Special Monthly Compensation is a higher rate of compensation VA pays to veterans, and to certain spouses, surviving spouses, and parents, who have specific needs or disabilities. Like other VA disability compensation, it is tax-free.
